name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,739

clue.text: Dope and beer? Bishop'll avoid that!

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so that letter stays out of the word

blocks.note: Bass is a well-known English brand of pale ale
B is the chess notation for bishop
surface padding: the contracted 'will' only makes the sentence read

explanation.surface: Drugs and booze are things a bishop would steer well clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the beer and let the bishop leave it. 'Dope' here means a fool, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and so is an ass: both are informal insults for a fool.

clue.text: Gangster, graduate, knight and saint

blocks.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A list of unlikely companions: a mobster, a graduate, a knight and a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: The list looks like four people; the last item is the definition. St Alban is honoured as the first British Christian martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban is a canonised martyr, venerated in the English city named after him, St Albans.

clue.text: Dad and sleek date getting high get out of it

indicators.note: someone getting high is out of their head, so the letters lose their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is a standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Father and a smooth companion getting stoned together, then making a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of it' reads as intoxicated, echoing 'getting high', but here it means leave in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is informal for running off quickly, just as 'get out of it' is a brusque order to clear off.

clue.text: Newly-arrived soldiers at the front reload

indicators.note: being placed at the front means this piece goes first, before the other one

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
something just come in is fresh

explanation.surface: New troops on the front line are busy reloading their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reload' sounds like guns, but it is the browser sense: refreshing a web page loads it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing refresh on a browser fetches the page anew, which is exactly what reloading means.

clue.text: Sexy chaps with guns like a boxer with no top on?

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and having no top means that letter is gone

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a boxer throws punches, so is punchy

explanation.surface: Muscular armed men looking like a shirtless boxer: a pin-up picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No top on' suggests bare-chested, but it just removes the first letter of the boxer's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy describes something earthy and sexually frank, a close informal synonym for sexy.

clue.text: Something you might wash with is soap

blocks.note: first meaning: a small cloth for washing the face
second meaning: smooth evasive talk, as in 'soft soap'

explanation.walkthrough: The bathroom picture pairs cloth and soap; the second meaning is figurative. In Britain a flannel is a face cloth, and flannel is also empty flattering talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is flattery used to persuade, and flannel is the British word for that same smooth, evasive chatter.

clue.text: Take drugs to get up? That's uncannily weird!

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means climbing from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: R, from Latin recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take
E is ecstasy, so two of them are drugs
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone takes pills to get going and finds the result deeply strange.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the prescription shorthand for 'take', from Latin recipe; after it flips, i.e. ('that is') is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes a strange, unsettling quality that seems unnatural, which is what uncannily weird conveys.

clue.text: One employed to help maintain a beehive?

definitions.text: One employed to help maintain a beehive?

blocks.clueFragment: One employed to help maintain a beehive?
blocks.note: surface reading: a worker in an apiary keeping bees
setter's reading: the tall bouffant hairdo of the 1960s, which needs a lot of fixing product

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: the beehive is the piled-up hairstyle, held in place by lacquer from a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive hairstyle only stays up with plenty of lacquer, so the product is employed to keep it in shape.

clue.text: Dramatic scene in story about black gold

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another
to be about something is to surround it, so the outer word wraps round a letter

blocks.note: a story is a tale
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A striking moment in a tale about oil, the black gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black gold' is a stock phrase for oil, but here it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking, often motionless grouping of figures, a picturesque scene as on a stage.

clue.text: Nurse with rig cut large extremity off a climber!

indicators.note: a thing cut is shortened, so it loses its final letter

blocks.note: to nurse is to tend
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A nurse amputating a big limb from a mountaineer: a grisly accident scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The climber sounds like a mountaineer but is a climbing plant; 'large extremity' wants to be a big limb, yet the definition starts at 'extremity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot a climbing plant sends out from its stem to grip supports.

clue.text: Feeling nausea due to being high as a kite?

definitions.text: Feeling nausea due to being high as a kite?

blocks.note: surface reading: heavily intoxicated on drugs

blocks.clueFragment: Feeling nausea due to being high
blocks.note: setter's reading: queasy because you are literally up in the sky, like a flying kite

explanation.walkthrough: 'High as a kite' is the idiom for stoned, but the setter means physically high, in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names motion sickness felt while flying, nausea brought on by being aloft in an aircraft.

clue.text: Joke which might be provided by child

blocks.note: first meaning: to tease or fool around, as in 'just kidding'
second meaning: a young person, informally

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a child telling a joke; in fact the same short word is a verb for joking and a noun for a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to jest or tease, and as a noun it is everyday slang for a youngster.

clue.text: Assassin detained in prison in Japan

indicators.note: someone detained is held inside, so the letters are held within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A hired killer locked up in a Japanese jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Japanese setting fits the answer neatly, which helps disguise that it is sitting in plain sight across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a covert agent in feudal Japan, trained in espionage and killing, hence an assassin.

clue.text: Prisoner not very bright duke cut down

blocks.note: a con is a convict
dense means stupid
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A dim-witted convict kills an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' reads as slain, but it means shortened, as a text is.
explanation.definitionFit: A condensed text has been abridged or shortened, reduced to fewer words while keeping its substance.

clue.text: Dry pal I will get blitzed with speed

indicators.note: blitzed means wrecked, whether bombed or drunk, so the letters are smashed up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teetotal friend confesses they will get wasted on amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the drug, and 'dry' like sober, but 'with speed' simply means quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with speed means doing it fast, an adverbial phrase matching quickly.

clue.text: Star map a gent ripped up without right

indicators.note: a thing ripped up is torn apart, so its letters are scattered and reordered
without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters sit around another

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man tears up a chart of the stars without having any right to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without right' reads as 'having no right', but 'without' means outside here: the letter goes in, not out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed figure drawn with a single line, a star shape.

clue.text: Blue European commie brought down

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling low
E is the abbreviation for European
a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: A dejected Continental communist was toppled from power.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue and red suggest colours or politics; blue is sad here, and red the communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to bring it down to a lesser height, so the past forms are equivalent.

clue.text: A sewer's in awfully tired state

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a messed-up order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A seamstress, or a drain, is in a terribly run-down condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' can be read as someone who sews or as a drain; neither sense matters, only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness is the condition of being exhausted, fatigue felt after long exertion.

clue.text: Pedal essentially pushed with less pressure to get in gear?

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letter is taken
less pressure means the abbreviation for pressure is subtracted from the word

blocks.note: the middle letter of the five
to push a button is to press it

explanation.surface: A driver easing off the pedal while changing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure. 'In gear' looks like a car but means wearing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothing, so someone in gear is clothed and ready.

clue.text: Easy-going nurse meets one breaking fast?

indicators.note: something breaking a thing splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: an Enrolled Nurse
the Roman numeral for one
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A relaxed nurse meets someone who has just ended their fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking fast' suggests breakfast; the fast is the forty days before Easter, split open to take the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and mild in judging others, which is how an easy-going person behaves.

clue.text: Articles written about concerning school in May?

definitions.note: the first name that goes with May, as in the former prime minister

indicators.note: things written about something are set around it, so they enclose the rest

blocks.note: the definite article
re means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for school
the indefinite article, the second of the two

explanation.surface: Pieces written on school matters during the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the month; it is the surname of Theresa May, UK prime minister 2016-19, whose first name is 'in May'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May led the British government, so her given name is found in the full name of that politician.

clue.text: Yen to punch sweet Hoskins? Good grief!

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so this letter is driven inside another word

blocks.note: a sweet person is a dear
Y is the abbreviation for the yen
Hoskins is the setter, who calls himself me

explanation.surface: Someone longs to hit the lovely Hoskins, who cries out in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is this puzzle's setter, so his name gives ME. 'Yen' could be a longing, but it is the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Deary me is a mild exclamation of dismay or surprise, interchangeable with good grief.

clue.text: Society girl on beer snorting coke is mess

indicators.note: snorting draws something up inside, so a letter is taken into the word

blocks.note: a debutante, a girl making her debut in high society
ale is beer
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A posh girl on the booze and snorting cocaine is a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coke' is cocaine, which shortens to C.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating failure or fiasco, a total mess.

clue.text: In period of darkness, blew a boat up

indicators.note: things blown up are shattered, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Under cover of night, a saboteur blows up a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The boat links to the tide idiom, and 'darkness' is the gloomy mood, not night.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a state of depression or decline, a dark and gloomy stretch of life.

clue.text: Man requiring you to separate colt from young cow

indicators.note: separating one thing from another takes it away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a calf is a young cow
C is the abbreviation for colt, as in racing form

explanation.surface: A farmer needs your help to keep a foal apart from a calf.
explanation.walkthrough: The colt is not an animal here but the letter C. Man stands for any short male name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alf is a familiar shortening of Alfred, so it serves as a man's name.

clue.text: Old American bum going around island watering hole

indicators.note: going around something encircles it, so the outer word wraps round a letter

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
ass is the American spelling for the backside
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An elderly American tramp wanders round an island's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A bum can be a tramp in the US, but here it is the backside, which Americans spell ass.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where water is found, a literal place for animals to drink.

clue.text: One's had a fill of Tory representatives!

indicators.note: something given a filling has another thing stuffed inside it

blocks.note: one is I, with the S of the possessive
Con is short for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone has had quite enough of Conservative MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a fill of' sounds like 'had a bellyful of', fed up; it means filled with.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or symbol standing for something else, so icons are representations of their subjects.

clue.text: Where one might find H readily available

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, the letter H is printed on the hot water fitting over a sink
second meaning: to be had whenever wanted, like beer from a barrel

explanation.walkthrough: H is slang for heroin, so the surface suggests drugs easily bought; really it is the letter marking hot on a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means obtainable at any time, as draught beer is, and H literally sits on the hot water fitting.

clue.text: Predict warning will be given to holy office

blocks.note: the golfer's shout of warning
a see is a bishop's office or diocese

explanation.surface: A prophet's warning is delivered to a church authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Fore is the cry golfers give to anyone in the path of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to know in advance what will happen, the same idea as predicting.

clue.text: Highly emotional after Celtic played away

indicators.note: coming after means following, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Celtic
a heated exchange is highly emotional

explanation.surface: Feelings ran high after Celtic, the Glasgow football club, played an away match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played away' is football for a match at the opponent's ground, but it is also British slang for being unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing away is a British euphemism for having an affair, which is being unfaithful to a partner.

clue.text: Doctor and old lady get on around ship

indicators.note: being around something encloses it, so the outer letters wrap the inner ones

blocks.note: an old lady is one's mother, ma
to get on is to grow older, to age
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A physician and an elderly woman board a ship together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb, as in to doctor the figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to tamper with information to make it look better, as with accounts or statistics.

clue.text: Drink Kitty mostly knocked back

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: puss is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: Kitty downs most of a drink in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking fast, fitting the definition, but it only flips the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to take liquid in small mouthfuls, an old-fashioned word for drinking.
